units: metres; character is 1.70 m tall, faces -Y, his left is +X, up is +Z

clips.name: ClimbUp
clips.note: starts on Wave frame 1 offset by standOffset; root motion carries him onto the block; ends exactly on DangleIdle f1

clips.name: Scared
clips.note: starts on DangleIdle f1, ends catch-ready

clips.name: CatchPlace
clips.note: starts on Scared last frame, ends exactly on DangleIdle f1

anchors.note: Place the character object at `stand` while Poof and Wave play and at `seat` from ClimbUp onward.  ClimbUp frame 1 already carries the standOffset in its root track, so the world pose is identical across the Wave -> ClimbUp cut.

seatBlock.note: Not a cube.  Two separate measurements set it: the approved DangleIdle plants his mitts out to |x| = 0.48, so the top face has to be ~1.0 m wide or both hands hang in mid air; and the block he sets down needs a clear landing strip outboard of that, which takes it to 1.16.  The 0.653 height is what makes his boots dangle 0.30 m clear of the floor.

timeline.hang: Scared frames 6-24 drifts from spawn to hangUntilCaught
timeline.carried: CatchPlace frames 11-44, riding on top of the two mitts
timeline.walkedDown: CatchPlace frames 44-57, on the right mitt alone
timeline.dropped: CatchPlace frames 57-63 (he lets go: a 0.30 m mitt cannot reach the seat top)

carryBlock.note: During the carry the block is placed on the top of the glove geometry each frame, which is why the catch reads as load-bearing.  The app can reproduce it by parenting the block to a midpoint between the two hand bones with a +0.13 z offset, or simply bake this path.

rig.rootMotion: Hips translation is baked into Poof, ClimbUp and the seated clips; do not add your own vertical offset.
rig.squashStretch: Hips bone SCALE is animated in Poof, ClimbUp, Scared and CatchPlace.  Keep bone inheritScale = full.

glb.axes: glTF Y-up: the Blender +Z (up) is glTF +Y, Blender -Y (facing) is glTF -Z.  three.js loads it upright with no fix-up.
glb.contents: character mesh + 24-bone armature + the six clips.  No plinth, lights, cameras or prop block: the app owns those.
glb.textures: single 1024x1024 WebP (EXT_texture_webp).  three.js GLTFLoader decodes it natively; no extra loader needed.
glb.geometryCompression: none -- draco/meshopt would make the app ship a decoder for a 7k-triangle character.
glb.sampleTimes: rebased to t=0 (tools/fix_times.mjs).  Blender writes frame/fps, so straight out of the exporter every clip started at t=1/30 and held its first pose for an extra frame -- 100 ms of hitch per idle loop.

skinRepair: The source Meshy rig binds most of each glove to <side>UpLeg, so raising an arm smears a brown ribbon from the mitt to the armpit.  It is repaired on import (fulcrum_rig.fix_hand_weights) and the repair is BAKED INTO THIS GLB -- do not re-import the original Meshy file.
